In summary, our research is concerned with
the transmission of monetary policy shocks to investment and capital prices in the U.S. economy.
the effects of unanticipated policy changes on real investment and the prices of fixed assets.
the effects of a monetary policy shock on real output, the price of capital goods, and the components of private investment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
monetary policy has significant effects on both the prices and quantities of investment.
a contractionary monetary policy shock has an overall negative effect on investment.

monetary policy shocks are transmitted to the real side of the economy through both the quantity and price channels, but the relative importance of each channel depends on the type of fixed investment considered.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the response of PFI to monetary policy is highly heterogeneous and, in some sectors, the effects on prices dominate those on quantities.
the effects of monetary policy shocks on PFI depend on the type of assets being considered and that the effects on prices tend to be more significant than those on quantities.
the effects on the real side of the economy are larger and longer-lived in the equipment sector than in the nonresidential structure sector, while price effects dominate the response in the latter.
The main takeaway from our work is that
monetary policy shocks have a differential impact on the various components of PFI.
a monetary policy tightening has a significant negative impact on investment and that the impact is larger in industries that are more dependent on external financing.
the aggregate response of PFI is driven by the behavior of equipment, which accounts for about 60 percent of total PFI.
